ConocoPhillips fell sharply yesterday (dropping $8.69 or 6.1% from $141.22 to $132.54) and has stayed near those lows today, likely driven by oil price weakness after Saudi Arabia signaled it would increase crude supplies via the Strait of Hormuz following a pipeline attack. The move eased supply-disruption fears that had pushed prices higher earlier in the week—US oil fell to $107/barrel today from levels that had supported the stock's brief rally to $141 on September 15th.

The broader geopolitical backdrop also shifted in a way that pressured prices: Trump signaled the U.S. may be nearing an end to its Iran conflict, and reports of potential peace talks with Tehran reduce the premium investors had been paying for the risk of Middle Eastern supply disruptions. While new U.S. oil development deals in Venezuela and tariff leverage against countries buying Russian oil could support energy supply long-term, the immediate driver was relief that the near-term supply crisis appears contained.
